title: Hebrews Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Hebrews 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: God spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets
He hath appointed heir of all things
questions.correctAnswer: God spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in Hebrews 1, found in Hebrews 1:1.

questions.question: Who has spoken unto us in these last days according to Hebrews 1?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Hebrews 1:2 where it says, 'Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son.'

questions.question: What has the Son been appointed as, according to Hebrews 1?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:2 states that He hath appointed heir of all things.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:3, what is the Son the brightness of?
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that the Son is 'the brightness of his glory' in Hebrews 1:3.

questions.question: What did the Son do when He had purged our sins?
options: Sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high
questions.correctAnswer: Sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Hebrews 1:3, stating that He 'sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:4, how is the Son described in relation to the angels?
options: He is equal to the angels
He is much better than the angels
He is less than the angels
He is a servant to the angels
questions.correctAnswer: He is much better than the angels
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:4 states, 'Being made so much better than the angels.'

questions.question: What has the Son obtained by inheritance according to Hebrews 1?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Hebrews 1:4 where it says He hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.

questions.question: In Hebrews 1:5, who is referred to as 'my Son'?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:5 asks, 'For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son?' indicating the reference is to the Son.

questions.question: What does God say He will be to the Son according to Hebrews 1:5?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And again, I will be to him a Father,' referring to the Son.

questions.question: Who did God speak to in time past according to Hebrews 1:1?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:1 states that God spake in time past unto the fathers.

questions.question: What is the Son described as in Hebrews 1:3?
options: The express image of his person
questions.correctAnswer: The express image of his person
questions.explanation: The text in Hebrews 1:3 describes the Son as 'the express image of his person.'

questions.question: True or False: God spoke by the prophets in time past.
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Hebrews 1:1 where it says God spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets.

questions.question: True or False: The Son was made lower than the angels.
questions.explanation: This is true as it is implied in Hebrews 1:4 where He is described as being made better than the angels.

questions.question: True or False: God said to the angels, 'Thou art my Son.'
questions.explanation: This is false because Hebrews 1:5 specifies that God did not say this to the angels but to the Son.

questions.question: True or False: The Son created the worlds according to Hebrews 1.
questions.explanation: This is false; while the Son is involved in creation, the verse states He made the worlds, not that this is a primary focus of the text.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:6, who are commanded to worship the firstbegotten Son brought into the world?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:6 states, 'And let all the angels of God worship him,' indicating the angels are commanded to worship the Son.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 1:7 promise will happen if God makes his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire as described in Hebrews 1:6?
options: They will serve as ministering spirits
They will be given dominion over the earth
They will become sons of God
questions.correctAnswer: They will serve as ministering spirits
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:7 says angels are made 'spirits' and 'ministers a flame of fire,' implying their role to serve, connecting to the worship command in 1:6.

questions.question: What is described as the sceptre of the Son's kingdom in Hebrews 1:8?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:8 states, 'a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom,' describing the nature of Christ's rule.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:8-9, what is the relationship between loving righteousness and being anointed with the oil of gladness?
options: Loving righteousness and hating iniquity results in anointing with the oil of gladness
Anointing with oil is unrelated to righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Loving righteousness and hating iniquity results in anointing with the oil of gladness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:9 links loving righteousness and hating iniquity to God anointing the Son with the oil of gladness above fellows.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 1:10 affirm the Son's role in creation?
options: He laid the foundation of the earth
He was created after the earth
questions.correctAnswer: He laid the foundation of the earth
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:10 states that the Lord laid the foundation of the earth, showing the Son's active role in creation.

questions.question: In practical Christian living, what does Hebrews 1:9 suggest about attitudes toward sin?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:9 highlights that the Son 'hated iniquity,' implying believers should also reject sin actively.

questions.question: What does the comparison between the Son and angels in Hebrews 1:4 imply for Christian faith?
options: The Son is superior to angels
questions.correctAnswer: The Son is superior to angels
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:4 states the Son is made so much better than angels, encouraging trust in His supreme authority.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:3, what action did the Son complete before sitting at the right hand of Majesty on high?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 explains the Son 'purged our sins' before sitting down, highlighting His role in salvation.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 1:2 describe the Son's appointment in relation to all things?
options: He is appointed heir of all things
He is the servant of prophets
questions.correctAnswer: He is appointed heir of all things
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:2 states the Son was appointed heir of all things, emphasizing His authority over creation.

questions.question: What practical principle about prayer and worship can be drawn from Hebrews 1:6?
options: Worship Christ as divine, following angelic example
questions.correctAnswer: Worship Christ as divine, following angelic example
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:6 shows angels worship the Son, teaching Christians to worship Christ as God.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 1:7 teach about the nature of angels and their function?
options: They are spirits and ministers of flame
They are kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: They are spirits and ministers of flame
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:7 describes angels as spirits and ministers like flames of fire, indicating their ministering role.

questions.question: How should Christians view righteousness based on the Son's example in Hebrews 1:9?
options: As something to love and pursue
questions.correctAnswer: As something to love and pursue
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:9 shows the Son loved righteousness, encouraging believers to also value righteousness highly.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 1:3 states that the Son is the express image of God's person and upholds all things by His powerful word.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 affirms the Son is 'the express image of his person' and sustains all things by His word.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 1:5 declares that God has never called any angel His Son.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:5 explicitly asks, 'For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son?' indicating no angel has been called Son as Christ has.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 1:10, the heavens were made by the angels' hands.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:10 states the heavens are the works of God's hands, not angels.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:11, what will happen to 'they' who shall wax old as a garment?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:11 states 'They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment;' showing that 'they' will perish.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 1:12 say will happen to the heavens and the earth, compared to a vesture?
options: They shall be folded up and changed
They shall be torn apart and destroyed
They shall be renewed without change
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be folded up and changed
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:12 says, 'And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed,' indicating the heavens and earth will be folded up like a garment and changed.

questions.question: In Hebrews 1:13, to which group is it said that God never said 'Sit on my right hand'?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:13 explicitly asks, 'But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand,' indicating that this was never said to any angel.

questions.question: Hebrews 1:14 calls angels what kind of spirits?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:14 describes angels as 'ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 1:11-12, how is the permanence of God described in contrast to creation?
options: God remains the same while creation perishes and changes
Both God and creation perish at the same time
Creation remains forever while God changes
God and creation are equally eternal
questions.correctAnswer: God remains the same while creation perishes and changes
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:11-12 contrasts 'They shall perish' and 'they shall be changed' with 'but thou remainest' and 'thou art the same,' emphasizing God's permanence.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the angels as described in Hebrews 1:14?
options: To minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation
To judge the wicked on earth
To lead armies in heavenly battles
questions.correctAnswer: To minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:14 states angels are 'ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation,' showing their role is service to believers.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'hegemon' used in Hebrews 1:3 mean?
questions.explanation: In Hebrews 1:3, the Greek term 'hegemon' (ἡγεμών) refers to a leader or ruler, highlighting Christ’s authority in upholding all things.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Hebrews 1:11-12 where the heavens and earth are compared to clothing?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:11 uses 'as doth a garment' which is a simile comparing the aging of creation to an old garment, a classic literary device.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Hebrews 1:10-12 when referring to the creation and its impermanence?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:10-12 closely quotes Psalm 102:25-27 which describes the creation perishing and God’s eternal nature.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to Hebrews 1:3's description of Christ as 'the brightness of his glory'?
questions.explanation: John 1:14 describes the Word becoming flesh and full of glory, paralleling Hebrews 1:3's depiction of Christ as the brightness of God's glory.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Hebrews 1:13 in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:12 directly precedes verse 13, as the chapter follows numerical order.

questions.question: In Hebrews 1:4, what is the reason given for Christ being made better than the angels?
options: He has obtained a more excellent name by inheritance
He is older than the angels
He is more powerful in battle
questions.correctAnswer: He has obtained a more excellent name by inheritance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:4 states Christ is better than angels 'as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.'

questions.question: How does Hebrews 1:5 use Old Testament scripture to distinguish the Son from angels?
options: By quoting Psalm 2:7 where God says, 'Thou art my Son'
By referring to the creation account
questions.correctAnswer: By quoting Psalm 2:7 where God says, 'Thou art my Son'
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:5 cites Psalm 2:7 to show that God said to the Son, 'Thou art my Son,' a statement not made to angels.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 1:14 teaches that angels are sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:14 states angels are 'ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation,' confirming their role as servants to believers.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 1:11 declares that God will perish just as the heavens and earth do.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:11 contrasts the perishing of creation with God's eternal nature, stating 'They shall perish; but thou remainest,' so God does not perish.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 1:3 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation is secured by the Son purging sins and then sitting at God's right hand
Salvation is achieved by human works and adherence to the law
Salvation is symbolic and does not involve actual cleansing of sin
Salvation is conditional upon angelic mediation
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is secured by the Son purging sins and then sitting at God's right hand
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 states that the Son 'when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high,' indicating the completed work of salvation by Christ's atonement and exaltation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning Christ’s divine sonship is taught in Hebrews 1:5?
options: Christ’s sonship is unique and not shared by angels
All angels are sons of God equally with Christ
Christ became Son of God only at his resurrection
Sonship is a title given to all faithful humans
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s sonship is unique and not shared by angels
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:5 contrasts Christ with angels by asking to which angel God ever said, 'Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee?', emphasizing the uniqueness of Christ's divine sonship.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 1:2 teach about God's revelation and Christ's role in creation?
options: God has spoken finally and fully through His Son, who also created the worlds
God revealed Himself only through the Old Testament prophets
Christ is a created being subordinate to God the Father
The worlds were made through angelic agents, not Christ
questions.correctAnswer: God has spoken finally and fully through His Son, who also created the worlds
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:2 declares that in these last days God has spoken by His Son, 'by whom also he made the worlds,' affirming Christ's role as creator and ultimate revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 1:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:12 says, 'but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail,' highlighting God's unchanging nature or immutability.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Hebrews 1:10 through the description of laying the earth's foundation?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:10 states, 'Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth,' demonstrating God's sovereign authority over creation.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 1:6 prepare for Christ's role in redemptive history?
options: By commanding all angels to worship the Son, it affirms Christ’s divine status
It denies Christ’s divinity by emphasizing angelic worship
It focuses solely on angelic hierarchy without Christ’s involvement
It depicts Christ as subordinate to angels
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding all angels to worship the Son, it affirms Christ’s divine status
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:6 commands, 'let all the angels of God worship him,' showing that Christ is to be worshiped, affirming his divine status and role in redemption.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Hebrews 1:4 make concerning Christ’s superiority?
options: It connects Christ’s exalted name as superior to angels to the fulfillment of messianic prophecy
It denies any superiority of Christ over angels
It teaches that angels and Christ share equal status in salvation
It refers only to angelic worship and not to Christ’s superiority
questions.correctAnswer: It connects Christ’s exalted name as superior to angels to the fulfillment of messianic prophecy
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:4 says Christ 'hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they,' which ties to messianic promises of Christ’s exalted status over angels.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 1:8 and 1:9 teach about Christ’s kingship and moral character?
options: Christ’s eternal kingship is characterized by righteousness and hatred of iniquity
Christ’s kingship is temporary and unrelated to moral qualities
Christ is a king only in name without moral implications
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s eternal kingship is characterized by righteousness and hatred of iniquity
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:8 declares Christ's throne is forever with a sceptre of righteousness, and 1:9 affirms he loved righteousness and hated iniquity, describing his moral perfection as king.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 1:11 and 1:12 teach about the contrast between creation and the Son’s nature?
options: Creation is perishable and transient, whereas the Son is unchanging and eternal
Creation and the Son are both eternal and unchanging
Creation is eternal but the Son is transient
Both creation and the Son will perish eventually
questions.correctAnswer: Creation is perishable and transient, whereas the Son is unchanging and eternal
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:11 says creation shall perish and wax old, but 1:12 states the Son is the same and his years shall not fail, distinguishing the Son's eternal nature from creation's decay.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 1:13 and 1:14 teach about Christ’s exaltation and the role of angels?
options: Christ’s exaltation above angels establishes his enemies as his footstool, while angels serve as ministering spirits for believers
Christ remains subordinate to angels who are rulers over believers
Angels are greater than Christ and execute his judgment
Christ and angels share equal authority and function
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s exaltation above angels establishes his enemies as his footstool, while angels serve as ministering spirits for believers
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:13 speaks of Christ sitting at God's right hand until enemies are subdued, and 1:14 describes angels as ministering spirits sent to help believers, showing the hierarchy and roles.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 1:2-3 teaches that Christ is merely a created being and not divine. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Christ is the appointed heir and agent of creation, reflecting divine nature and power
Christ is a created angelic being subordinate to God
Christ is a prophet without divine status
Christ is a human exalted by God but not divine
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is the appointed heir and agent of creation, reflecting divine nature and power
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:2 teaches Christ made the worlds and is heir of all things, and 1:3 describes him as brightness of glory and upholding all things by power, affirming his deity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 1:7 teach about the nature and function of angels?
options: Angels are spirits and ministers, created as flames of fire for service
Angels are immortal gods competing with Christ
Angels are human souls who have died
Angels are symbolic representations with no real existence
questions.correctAnswer: Angels are spirits and ministers, created as flames of fire for service
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:7 says, 'Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire,' indicating their created nature as ministering spirits.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Hebrews 1:9 through the description of Christ's anointing?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:9 says Christ loved righteousness and hated iniquity, and was anointed with oil of gladness above fellows, emphasizing his holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's progressive revelation is taught in Hebrews 1:1?
options: God revealed Himself in various ways through the prophets before finally speaking by His Son
God revealed Himself fully and finally only through the law of Moses
God’s revelation was limited to a single event
God has ceased all revelation after the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God revealed Himself in various ways through the prophets before finally speaking by His Son
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:1 states God spoke 'at sundry times and in divers manners... by the prophets,' indicating progressive revelation culminating in the Son.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Hebrews 1:3 and 1:10 form regarding Christ's identity and role?
options: Christ is both the agent of creation and the radiance of God's glory sustaining all things
Christ is only a moral teacher without creative power
Christ is a created being subordinate to God’s creative work
Christ’s role is limited to earth and does not include sustaining creation
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is both the agent of creation and the radiance of God's glory sustaining all things
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 describes Christ as 'upholding all things by the word of his power,' and 1:10 declares he laid the earth’s foundation, identifying him as Creator and sustainer.
